title: n=8 cycle-length dominance: scale-rotation OSCILLATES, not monotone
question: Does rule 110 STAY the dominant (longest mean cycle) rule at n=8, confirming the n=4->n=6 rotation as a one-step event?
engine: pure hexa-lang. n=8 periodic ECA ring (256 states), 256 starts × forward up to 300 steps, first-repeat cycle length.

rule_30_life.note: DOMINANT again at n=8 — reclaims from rule110

rule_110_life.note: drops from n=6 dominance (7.75) to 2nd place

rule_90_xor.note: XOR-linear collapses at even n (even-N bipartite artifact, cf H_297)

falsifier_eval.F334_1_RULE110_STAYS_DOMINANT: FAIL — rule110 (13.92) is overtaken by rule30 (35.89) at n=8
falsifier_eval.F334_2_ROTATION_IS_ONE_STEP: FAIL — the n=4->n=6 rotation is NOT a one-step event; n=8 reverts to rule30 → OSCILLATION
falsifier_eval.F334_3_BIJECTION_PERSISTS: PASS — rule105 == rule150 byte-identical (3.859) at n=8, bijection class stable across n

verdict_derived: 🔴 FALSIFIED (on H1) + OSCILLATION DISCOVERY — rule110 does NOT stay dominant at n=8; rule30 reclaims dominance with a dramatic mean cycle length 35.89 (vs 6.25 at n=4). The dominant rule OSCILLATES: rule30 (n=4) → rule110 (n=6) → rule30 (n=8). The pattern tracks the integer structure of the ring size: rule30 (chaotic class III) dominates at n=2^k (4, 8 — pure powers of two), while rule110 (universal class IV) dominated at n=6 (=2×3). This refines H_333 scale-rotation from 'monotone rotation' to 'n-parity-dependent oscillation' — the cycle-length leader is a function of the ring's prime factorization, not a fixed rule property.
structural_vs_dynamical: DYNAMICAL kernel, scale-rich (n=8, 256 states) — and at THIS scale rule30 chaotic gives a genuinely long mean cycle (35.89), confirming H_327's prediction that dynamical signals sharpen at richer scale. The new finding is that 'which rule is richest' is itself n-conditional via ring-size number theory.
honest_limits: Three n only (4, 6, 8); n=10, 12 needed to confirm the 2^k vs 2×odd hypothesis (n=12=2^2×3, n=16=2^4 are the decisive next tests)
300-step cap; rule30 mean 35.89 well under, but some long-cycle starts may be truncated — a cap sweep would harden
Ring-size number theory hypothesis (rule30@2^k vs rule110@2×odd) is a POST-HOC reading of 3 data points; n=10 (2×5) should give rule110 if the hypothesis holds
Only 5 rules; the dominance could rotate to a 6th rule at some n
discovery_note: scale-rotation이 oscillation으로 정련됨. dominant rule이 ring size n의 prime factorization 함수일 가능성 — rule30(chaotic)@n=2^k, rule110(universal)@n=2×odd. n=10/12/16 측정이 결정적 후속.
